top_categories.workout_context: 93ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Eroica Germania's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before August.
At Eroica Germania, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Eroica Germania. Train it until it feels boring.
75 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.

Road-specific control matters at Eroica Germania. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 75 miles.
7,053ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
7,053ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 7,053ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Low-cadence force work supports 7,053ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
76–85% FTP for extended efforts. At Eroica Germania, tempo is the floor you'll live on. Make it feel easy.
